posts.author: Ron Michael
posts.content_md:
I Just couldn't stay away from the ruby laser forever. So I shot this one using the plates I got from Lon, Thanks Lon, I finally got around to trying them out and they are still good!: [http://holographyforum.org/phpBB2/viewtopic.php?t=3788](http://holographyforum.org/phpBB2/viewtopic.php?t=3788)

2/14/07: Subjects 12 inches away from hologram.

1.1joule at 12ns and sm-6 and pyrochrome process. 

![Image](http://www.rotorwave.com/8x10.jpg)

posts.author: Ron Michael
posts.content_md: Thanks. I see you are also a ruby laser aficionado. You did nice work on your own fabricated design. My first holos were on a 60mj mopa using three 1/4 inch x 3 inch long rods. It made sharp images of toy helicopters without need for a table. It was cool to look on top of the forward blade and also see the underneath side of it by shifting your head.

posts.author: Ron Michael
posts.content_md:
To answer your questions:

yes, I used some some modified rangefinders since they were cheap about 180 dollars a piece at the time. Here is a link:[http://www.rotorwave.com/rw_mopa2.htm](http://www.rotorwave.com/rw_mopa2.htm)

Film size was 3x5.

Static model. No moving objects.

I'm afraid that valentines present was given away. I only took a quick picture of it.

posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md: Hey Ron, could you tell me the expiration date on the Agfa 8E75HD plates you used for the hologram above? I have some plates that expired (supposedly) in 1996, and was wondering if my efforts to use them will be an exercise in futility. I also have some old Kodak SO-253 on film base.

posts.author: Ron Michael
posts.content_md: These plates expired 2000. I have some Agfa 8e75hd film that expired in 1996 and it is excellent. I sure it's also a question batches and of enviromentals as well. I found some of my 2000 plates to be less sensitive to the 1996 film but overall I'm still pleased with them.
